hints.title: Negative Elements Subarray Sum Obstacle
hints.text: Because numbers can be negative, a sliding window cannot monotonically shrink when a sum is exceeded. Examining all subarrays takes quadratic time. How can recording cumulative totals from the start allow you to count matching slices in a single pass?

hints.title: Prefix Difference Frequency Counting
hints.text: A slice between indices i and j has sum equal to the difference of their running totals. If running sum minus target has appeared earlier, every previous occurrence marks the start of a valid slice.

hints.title: Single Pass Running Total Matching Procedure
hints.text: Initialize count to 0, current_sum to 0, and record initial state with 0 mapped to count 1. Iterate through each number, adding it to current_sum. Check how many times current_sum minus k has appeared and add that frequency to count. Then increment the frequency of current_sum in your record. Return count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 2 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass prefix sum difference frequency tracking in O(N) time and space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing or sliding through all O(N^2) subarrays takes quadratic time. Because elements can be negative, two-pointer shrinking fails to preserve monotonicity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using O(N) memory to store prefix sum frequencies reduces the search from O(N^2) to an optimal O(N) pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Initializing prefix_counts[0] = 1 to handle subarrays starting at index 0 and explaining why sliding window fails when negative numbers exist.
